note: API effect table (D-15, API-06, plan 03-13): for every public function, its header, its success behaviour, its check precedence (first failing class wins) and one row per refusal status with the state effect, the out parameters a refusal writes and the test ids that assert that status. The gate step api-effects (tools/check/api-effects.cmake) ties it to core/include/ivs/ivs_status.h, data/expected/api-statuses.ids, the IVS_API declarations of core/include/ivs/*.h (D-06 symbol list) and data/expected/tests/*.ids; tests-inventory proves each cited id ran in both presets. Residual (OQ-5): the step proves a cited id exists in an inventory, not that the case asserts that status; each cited case asserts its own status in its source. Status names are the macro names of ivs_status.h.

calls.name: ivs_machine_run
calls.on_ok: Runs a POWERED machine to the absolute target req->target_ticks in master ticks (D-01): while machine time is below the target it steps one CPU unit through the internal step seam, so it ends at the first unit boundary at or after the target (run.target.ends-at-first-boundary-ge-target, run.target.on-boundary-no-overshoot); a target at or below now runs nothing (run.target.already-reached). The report holds the stop reason, the CPU run state and fault reason at exit, now_ticks, overshoot_ticks = max(now - target, 0) (run.overshoot.equals-now-minus-target), elapsed_ticks and units_executed. No state is kept between calls; run(now + 1) is exactly one unit (run.single-step.equals-seam). Output buffers (D-02, D-03, D-06): video and audio go to caller-owned buffers named in the request; the core keeps no pointer. From plan 05-06 the real audio layout is PSG levels (IVS_OUTPUT_FORMAT_PSG_LEVELS_V1, 15,060 bytes per frame) and the real video layout is still NONE (video of any capacity is accepted and gets nothing, run.buffers.real-layout-audio): a call with an audio buffer of at least the requirement delivers one 4-byte sample A, B, C, 0 per PSG chip step (16 master ticks, an absolute grid from reset) to the buffer, reports audio_bytes_written and audio_first_index (the samples emitted before the call, so the streams of consecutive calls concatenate to the stream of one call), never writes past the delivered count, and an instance without a buffer ends in the byte-identical state (run.buffers.audio-real, psg.buffers.state-independent-of-buffer); a synthetic layout through the internal env seam whose audio format is not PSG levels delivers nothing, as in Phase 4. A capacity of exactly bytes_per_frame x (max(target - now, 0) / nominal_frame_ticks + 1) runs (run.buffers.exact-fit-video, run.buffers.exact-fit-audio, run.buffers.exact-fit-both, run.buffers.zero-layout, through the internal env seam with a synthetic layout), and the public call equals the seam given an equal env (run.buffers.entry-points-equal). A NULL buffer with capacity 0 means the channel is not requested (D-17, plan 05-02): no check, no byte, no state change whatever the layout requires, and the run equals the same call under a zero layout (run.buffers.null-zero-not-requested); a nonzero capacity below the requirement, and a non-NULL buffer with capacity 0 against a layout that needs bytes, are still refused (run.buffers.nonzero-too-small-refused). The request v2 appends a third caller-owned buffer, psg_log with psg_log_capacity, for the PSG register-write log (D-14, plan 05-02): it is read only when req->struct_size covers it (a v1-sized caller of IVS_RUN_REQUEST_V1_SIZE bytes reads as NULL and 0, run.struct.request-v1-caller), its requirement is psg_log_bytes_per_frame x (max(target - now, 0) / nominal_frame_ticks + 1), and the report v2 appends audio_first_index, psg_log_bytes_written and psg_log_first_index, written only inside the caller's struct_size (a v1-sized report of IVS_RUN_REPORT_V1_SIZE bytes gets exactly those bytes, run.struct.report-v1-caller; audio_first_index and audio_bytes_written follow the audio stream from plan 05-06). From plan 05-08 the write log is real (D-13, D-14): the layout publishes psg_log_records_per_frame 2,152 (W_log = ceil(59,736 / 28) + ceil(468 / 28) + 1, 34,432 bytes per frame slot, ivs_info v3), one 16-byte record per guest write to $01F0..$01FF is delivered in order from byte 0 of psg_log (tick, raw 16-bit value, address low nibble, source, reserved; psg.log.framing), the report gives psg_log_bytes_written and psg_log_first_index (the records logged before the call, so the logs of consecutive calls concatenate to the log of one call, psg.slice.log-split), a call without a log buffer logs into a counting sink and ends in the byte-identical state with the same domain-19 chain, and a never-expected shortfall (fewer than 16 bytes left before a unit) ends the run with IVS_STOP_INTERNAL at the last whole boundary (psg.buffers.log-safety-net). Input (D-12..D-15, plan 04-11): the request carries a caller-owned array of 32-byte ivs_input_event level samples (logical switch words indexed by PSG port), nondecreasing by at_tick; the core keeps no pointer and no queue. Exit tests come first; only when a unit will begin is every not yet applied event with at_tick <= the unit's start applied in array order, and nothing is applied at exit, so an event takes effect at the first unit boundary whose start is at or after its at_tick (run.input.one-event). The report returns input_consumed, input_failing_index IVS_INPUT_INDEX_NONE, input_floor_tick (start of the last begun unit + 1, instance state in the INPUT row) and controller_now; each applied event advances the INPUT log h(n+1) = SHA-256(h(n) || be64(at_tick) || be32 words), h0 = SHA-256("IVS-INPUT-LOG-V1"), checked against literals made with printf and cmake -E sha256sum (run.input.one-event). Equal ticks keep array order (run.input.equal-ticks); an event at a slice target applies in the next call (run.input.at-target); events inside the overshoot window wait for the next call and any slicing with the resubmitted suffix gives the one-call state (run.input.overshoot-window); with IVS_RUN_F_STOP_ON_HALT and the CPU HALTED a call stops before applying anything (run.input.halt-stops-first); reset returns the row to h0 (run.input.reset); instances do not share input (run.input.isolation); 65536 events are accepted (run.input.event-count-cap-ok); words below the profile's input.controllers carry input and zero words above it are accepted (run.input.extra-word-zero-ok, plan 04-12). From plan 05-05 the words are guest-visible (D-01, D-04): each applied event derives the pull-down masks of the two PSG ports from the words and the profile's control table, and a CPU read of $01FE or $01FF returns the idle byte XOR the OR of the line masks of every closed control (input mode; the stored latch in output mode), indexed by PSG port; a stand-in program that reads the ports sees the events, so the register trace, the CPU, MEM and composite digests and the guest RAM differ with and without events while the INPUT digest chain stays a function of the accepted script alone (run.input.guest-visible, D-01).

notes: D-04: stops are not refusals. A run that executes returns IVS_OK with stop_reason TARGET, CPU_HALTED (only with IVS_RUN_F_STOP_ON_HALT), GUEST_FAULT or INTERNAL, a pure function of the exit state in the order INTERNAL, fault, halt, target (run.stop.halt-flag, run.stop.halt-no-flag, run.stop.guest-fault, run.stop.fault-sticky, run.stop.fault-before-halt, run.stop.internal-step-refused). A FAULTED CPU is never stepped; a unit that does not advance time ends the loop.

D-05: a refusal writes only struct_size and refusal_reason (IVS_REASON_RUN_* 34..43 and 55..57, IVS_REASON_INPUT_* 44..54, IVS_REASON_HANDLE; input_failing_index too for 48..54), and nothing into a report that is itself the cause, that overlaps the bytes the handle names or that overlaps an output buffer; no refusal writes a byte into either buffer. Named faults RUN_TARGET_UNCHECKED, RUN_STOP_BEFORE_OVERSHOOT, RUN_FAULT_STEPS, RUN_BUDGET_CARRY, RUN_CAPACITY_AFTER_STEP, OUTBUF_PARTIAL_WRITE and, for input (plan 04-11), INPUT_APPLY_AT_RUN_START, INPUT_LOG_SLICE_RELATIVE_TICK, INPUT_NO_FLOOR_CHECK, INPUT_STATIC_CARRY, RUN_EVENT_AT_TARGET_ONLY, RUN_EVENTS_UNCHECKED (data/expected/faults/run.ids).

D-06 (plan 04-10): the capacity requirement is an upper bound per channel, bytes_per_frame x (max(target - now, 0) / nominal_frame_ticks + 1), counting the frame the overshoot of the last unit may complete. The struct sizes grow with Phase 4 (request 64 bytes on LP64 after plan 04-11, report 112); plan 04-13 pins them, after which the A-02 growth rule applies.

D-19, A-04 (plan 05-02): the minimum accepted struct_size is the pinned v1 size (request IVS_RUN_REQUEST_V1_SIZE 64 on LP64, report IVS_RUN_REPORT_V1_SIZE 112), never sizeof of the grown struct; request v2 is 80 bytes (psg_log at 64, psg_log_capacity at 72), report v2 136 (audio_first_index 112, psg_log_bytes_written 120, psg_log_first_index 128). A request is read only as far as its struct_size covers, the report is written as min(struct_size, 136) bytes with struct_size set to that count, and a refusal writes only inside the v1 prefix (run.struct.request-v1-caller, run.struct.report-v1-caller, run.struct.request-v2-fields, run.struct.report-v2-fields, run.struct.tail-nonzero).

The instance is not written, machine time does not advance, nothing is allocated and the call touches no file or clock; two saves of one instance are byte-identical.

calls.name: ivs_snapshot_describe
calls.on_ok: Checks the len bytes at buf in the order of docs/formats/ivsn-v1.md up to and including the SHA-256 trailer and the form of the profile id, without any instance, and writes the full v1 report: reason 0, the format and schema versions, total_bytes (4,299 for the first profile), byte_offset 0, section_index 0xFFFFFFFF, kind 0, the profile id, the parameter digest and the composite digest of the writer and the three image slot records (kind slot index plus one, loaded, length_bytes and SHA-256 as the snapshot states them). Nothing is read past len, nothing is allocated, nothing but the report is written and the call touches no file or clock (plan 08-12, D-13, D-14).

precedence.checks: rep NULL, or rep->struct_size below IVS_SNAPSHOT_REPORT_V1_SIZE or above IVS_STRUCT_SIZE_MAX (nothing written)
buf NULL with len above 0 (reason 58), then the report overlapping the first min(len, IVS_SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES) bytes of buf (reason 59)

the section count is not 7 (reason 68)

the section table: an unknown, repeated, skipped or descending domain, a nonzero byte among the three zero bytes, a first offset other than 612, a section that does not begin where the one before ends, a length that does not fit before the trailer, or a last section that does not end 32 bytes before the total (reason 69, with the index of the entry)
the SHA-256 trailer differs from the digest of every earlier byte (reason 70); checked after the structure, so a structural defect with a wrong trailer is the structural reason

the profile id field: no NUL in its 64 bytes, a byte after the first NUL, or a byte before it that is not printable ASCII (reason 71); judged after the trailer, an empty or unregistered id of good form is accepted

notes: Instance-free: no handle, no instance. The reader never reads a byte past len and every length and offset in the bytes is compared with len before the byte it names is read; the section table check (reason 69) and the form of the profile id (reason 71) come after the header checks and before and after the trailer as docs/formats/ivsn-v1.md says. A refusal by an unusable report struct writes nothing. Every other refusal writes only reason, byte_offset, section_index and the header facts the supplied length let it read (format_version at 12 bytes, total_bytes at 16, schema_version at 24); every other member of the report keeps the caller's value. The report is a v1 out struct of 360 bytes: a caller struct larger than that keeps its tail. The snapshot is exact-build state: describe says what a snapshot claims to be, never that it restores.

calls.name: ivs_machine_snapshot_restore
calls.on_ok: Validates the whole snapshot (the container as describe judges it, the identity of the profile and of the three image slots against the instance, every section length, array count and frame, the CPU, STIC and PSG states through their validators, the phase and the clock range, the derived invariants) and only then replaces the state of the instance with the state the snapshot holds: the STATE rows of the digest field table are decoded into the instance, the PAD rows are zeroed, no BOUND or IMAGE row is written (the handle, the profile of the instance, the committed image structure, the three slot records and the image arrays stay), and the phase becomes POWERED (plan 08-13, D-14, D-15, D-41). A restore is allowed in every phase: an OFF instance with its images loaded is the normal fresh target and a POWERED one is rewound. The report, when given, is written in full as describe writes it. Nothing is allocated and the call touches no file or clock.

precedence.checks: rep not NULL with struct_size below IVS_SNAPSHOT_REPORT_V1_SIZE or above IVS_STRUCT_SIZE_MAX (nothing written)

a section length that differs from the derived length (80), an array count that differs from the table (77), a frame, a device state that its validator refuses, a phase other than POWERED or a clock above 2 to the power 63 (78), a derived invariant that does not hold (79), in that order

notes: Validate everything, then commit (D-15): the sections are decoded into a probe of a few hundred bytes and judged there, and only then does a commit with no refusal path write the instance, so a refusal leaves every byte of the instance as it was (whole-storage memcmp, rows of every family) and writes only the report. The digest fields of the header (the composite and the seven section digests) are informational and never checked; the trailer is integrity, not authenticity, and a snapshot whose trailer was recomputed is judged by the validators and the invariants. The report is optional (rep may be NULL). A refusal writes reason, byte_offset, section_index and the header facts the length let the reader see, as describe does, and kind for a refusal about an image slot; an unusable report struct, and a refusal while the report overlaps the instance, write nothing. The caller keeps its own output buffers and resubmits its input events from the restored applied-event count.
